title: A Baby Insect Has Real Gears in Its Legs (30 Microseconds Apart)

scenes.text: This baby insect has real mechanical gears in its legs.
It's a young Issus, a plant hopper from European gardens. Each leg has a gear strip with 10 to 12 teeth.
The teeth lock together, so both legs push at the same moment. Within 30 microseconds.
Nerves are far too slow for that. A nerve signal lasts one to two milliseconds, dozens of times too long.
So cogs time the jump, not the brain.
And when it becomes an adult, the gears vanish.

description:
This baby insect has real mechanical gears in its legs.
Young Issus planthoppers have gear strips with 10 to 12 teeth on their hind legs that keep both legs in sync within 30 microseconds. Adults lose them.
What else in nature do you think uses gears?

first_comment: Scientists don't yet know why the gears disappear at the final molt. What's your guess?
